explanation: The merged Candidate makes simultaneous shared text and execution output the primary interaction, so removing WebSocket-style state synchronization would turn it into a different single-user or delayed product.

The Spec keeps WebSocket flow, client-server synchronization and input ordering in Learner Focus; code execution, error handling and basic UI stay in Agent Support; persistence, authentication and IDE-grade features remain excluded. The listed Decisions expose real concurrency and deployment tradeoffs without expanding the MVP.
